title: List of existing food additives
journal: Japan Food Chemical Research Foundation, English translation of the Japanese list, revision of 25 August 2025
funder: not stated. The page is published by the Japan Food Chemical Research Foundation and states that it translates the Japanese list first compiled by public notice of the Minister for Health and Welfare on 16 April 1996 and since revised, the latest revision announced by the Consumer Affairs Agency.
result: Existing food additives are substances of natural origin permitted for use and distribution in Japan as an exception to the designation system of the Food Sanitation Act, because of long use in Japan; the status was set by the 1995 amendment of the Act, which made all additives subject to designation. Entry 76 of the list is xanthan gum, described as a substance composed mainly of polysaccharides obtained from the cultured solution of bacteria belonging to Xanthomonas. Five entries are lecithins: 153 vegetable lecithin, mainly lecithin from rape seeds or soybeans; 312 yolk lecithin, from egg yolk; 251 fractionated lecithin, mainly sphingomyelin, phosphatidylinositol, phosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidylcholine from vegetable or yolk lecithin; 119 enzymatically modified lecithin, mainly phosphatidylglycerol from either; and 122 enzymatically decomposed lecithin, mainly phosphatidic acid and lysolecithin from either. The revision announced by the Consumer Affairs Agency on 25 August 2025 removed 30 additives and left 327 on the list.
